summary: The build can start against an existing M30-or-higher cluster using the installed DocumentDB skills, MongoDB Node.js driver, and MCP tools. DiskANN indexing and retrieval are documented. End-to-end execution still needs locally supplied database and model credentials, dependency-version checks, and explicit LlamaIndex session-memory wiring. The largest product friction is inconsistent guidance: current Learn pages and installed skills disagree on deployment API versions, retryable writes, endpoints, and full-text search. No resources or data were changed.
summary_points: The build can start with the prompt review’s existing-cluster, local CLI, and synthetic-data assumptions.
DiskANN requires M30 or higher, and its index and query syntax are verified.
The documented LlamaIndex vector-store connector is Python-only; this Node.js app should expose MongoDB-driver retrieval through an agent tool.
Database configuration, model credentials, and the exact LlamaIndex dependency and memory APIs remain unverified.
Current documentation conflicts with installed skills on API versions, retryable writes, endpoint examples, and text-search recommendations.
Missing infrastructure CLIs and mongosh do not prevent this sample because provisioning is out of scope and driver/MCP alternatives exist.

confusions.question: What does a connection string look like: scheme, host suffix, port, and the options it must carry?
confusions.cold_answer: mongodb+srv://<username>:<url-encoded-password>@<cluster>.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com/?tls=true&authMechanism=SCRAM-SHA-256&retryWrites=false&maxIdleTimeMS=120000; no explicit SRV port; allow TCP 10260.
confusions.grounded_answer: This is a supported cluster-specific form, and the rename did not change existing URIs. The current Node.js quickstart shows the global form <cluster>.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com with TLS, SCRAM-SHA-256, retrywrites=false, and maxIdleTimeMS=120000. Default connectivity uses 10260; query-from-any-node can require additional SRV-advertised ports. Copy the actual portal URI rather than synthesizing a host. confusions.question: Which MongoDB wire protocol or server versions are supported, and which commonly used features are not?
confusions.cold_answer: Target 7.0; choices include 5.0–8.0; avoid mapReduce, server-side JavaScript, cross-shard transactions, and unrestricted administration; use cosmosSearch instead of Atlas vector syntax.
confusions.grounded_answer: Versions 5.0, 6.0, 7.0, and 8.0 are documented; current quickstarts select 8.0. The compatibility matrix treats mapReduce as deprecated and JavaScript operators as deprecated in 8.0. Cross-shard multi-document ACID transactions are supported according to the Atlas comparison. Managed administration is restricted and vector retrieval uses cosmosSearch.

Scheme validation alone is insufficient: use the actual managed mongodb+srv URI, TLS and compatible authentication, and let the driver detect DNS/auth/network failures without leaking credentials.

confusions.question: Does Azure DocumentDB automatically provide LlamaIndex session memory, and how should the sample persist it?
confusions.cold_answer: No automatic attachment; explicitly key memory by sessionId, optionally persist sessions with a unique index and updateOne upsert, load before retrieval and save afterward.
confusions.grounded_answer: The architecture is supported: documented agent examples explicitly manage conversation history by session identifiers, and DocumentDB supports unique indexes and updateOne/upsert. The LlamaIndex guide does not supply automatic session-memory wiring and its vector-store connector is Python-only. A sessions collection is an application design, not a built-in LlamaIndex persistence contract; exact JavaScript memory serialization and agent APIs remain unverified.

information_gaps.title: Actual target readiness
information_gaps.description: The inventory identifies a default MCP profile but not its cluster resource ID, M30+ tier, application URI, network route, or ingestion/index privileges. Skills establish the prerequisites, not that the supplied environment satisfies them. The user must confirm the intended cluster without exposing credentials.

information_gaps.title: Retryable-write support matrix
information_gaps.description: documentdb-connection, documentdb-azure-deployment, and the native Node.js quickstart use false; documentdb-driver and the Node.js OIDC guide use true; Amazon migration guidance says to remove false. No retrieved source reconciles support by authentication, operation, version, or topology. Use the native vector sample’s false setting, but do not claim the service-wide support question is settled.

information_gaps.title: Recommendation ranking and quality
information_gaps.description: Vector and aggregation syntax are documented, but no source specifies how this retail sample should combine co-purchase counts, semantic similarity, and session preferences. Catalog size, duplicate-line semantics, normalization, deterministic tie-breaking, and fallback behavior when fewer than five items remain require explicit application assumptions.

information_gaps.title: Local DiskANN parity
information_gaps.description: The local skill and development-loop tutorial document the gateway image and CRUD connection, but do not establish that the selected local image implements managed DiskANN with identical behavior. Local CRUD tests cannot replace an authorized M30+ integration check.

information_gaps.title: Model access and ingestion budget
information_gaps.description: The LlamaIndex guide documents provider configuration, but the inventory does not verify credentials, deployments, quotas, or embedding costs. The builder must choose whether to embed a small catalog once rather than all 20,000 order records and implement bounded provider calls.
